stories.title: Resolved-sideband micromotion sensing in trapped
stories.description: We have investigated excess micromotion for a Yb$$^+$$ ion in a Paul trap. In the presence of light modulated by excess micromotion, we calculate the cooling florescence spectrum of the 369.53 nm transition by finding the steady periodic state solution of the Lindblad master equation including the time-dependent Hamiltonian. We have shown that applying a 369.53 nm laser for specific RF parameters does not resolve efficiently micromotion sidebands. To sense well-resolved sidebands micromotion, we solve the Lindblad equation for the four-level optical transitions of the cooling cycle by incorporating the introduced time-dependent Hamiltonian and the branching ratio for spontaneous decay rates at the low intensity limit. However, in the weak-driving regime the rate equation under adiabatic approximation is implemented to detect the excess micromotion effects on the cooling florescence as a function of the repump detuning. This steady state florescence rate of P-state based on the rate equation approach leads to results in agreement with the Lindblad master equation, but with much less computational effort and no numerical issues. We show that by scanning the detuning of the repump laser, the cooling spectrum could be applied as an efficient micromotion sensor at $$\Omega _\mathrm{{c/r}}=0.1 \Gamma _\mathrm{{P/B}}$$. Our comprehensive discussion provides a theoretical and practical framework to predict the accurate experimental observations of sideband micromtion sensing in the trapped Yb$$^+$$ ion which can be used and also extended.

stories.title: Oncogenic signalling and host immunocompetency govern senescent cell clearance and systemic inflammation in a mouse model of oncogene-induced senescence
stories.description: Senescence is a stress-induced program defined by permanent cell-cycle arrest and a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Defective clearance of senescent cells promotes inflammation, tissue dysfunction, and ageing, yet determinants of their elimination remain poorly understood. Here, we model oncogene-induced senescence in the hematopoietic system by transplanting BrafV600E- or BrafΔN-expressing hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells into recipients with distinct immune backgrounds. BrafV600E induces a stronger senescence program and more aggressive disease than BrafΔN. Survival depends on oncogene-expressing cell burden and host immunity: immunocompetent, lower-burden mice clear oncogene-expressing cells and survive long-term, whereas higher-burden mice show checkpoint upregulation, T-cell exhaustion, and early death. NSG, Rag1KO, and lymphocyte-depleted hosts fail to clear these cells, developing sustained inflammation and bone marrow failure. Rapamycin administration attenuates senescence-associated features and improves survival. These findings identify oncogenic intensity and adaptive immune competence as coupled determinants of senescent-cell fate, with implications for chronic inflammation and senescence-targeted therapies. Defective clearance of senescent cells contributes to chronic systemic inflammation and tissue damage. Here, the authors adopt a mouse model of oncogene-induced senescence and report that oncogenic signal strength and the adaptive immune response govern senescent cell clearance, ultimately influencing animal survival

stories.title: VentVirGenomes: A Global Ocean Hydrothermal Vent Virus Genome Dataset for Exploring Diversity, Function, and Host Interactions
stories.description: Ocean hydrothermal vents constitute chemically driven oases of life that fundamentally differ from photosynthesis-based ecosystems. Recognized as one of Earth’s most extreme environments, they serve as key systems for investigating the origins of life. To elucidate the still poorly understood diversity of viruses and virus–host interactions in these settings, we analyzed 405 globally distributed metagenomic samples from ocean hydrothermal systems across seven habitat types and depths ranging from 0 to 5000 m. From these data, we constructed the Global Ocean Hydrothermal Vent Virus Genome Dataset (VentVirGenomes), which comprises 392,166 viral contigs and 332,833 viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs). Taxonomic classification at the realm level could be estimated for 68.37% of these vOTUs, with Caudoviricetes representing the dominant class. Furthermore, we identified 79,317 predicted virus-host linkages. The VentVirGenomes provides a foundational resource for advancing research into the diversity, evolution, and ecological functions of viral and microbial communities within global hydrothermal vent ecosystems.
